thread:
lena: quick heads-up — intermittent JSON parse errors in the iOS streaming client after session resume. ~1% of sessions. Crash: JSONSerialization fails with "Unexpected character" on small streaming responses.

sam: I ran into that yesterday. root cause looked like chunk boundaries splitting a multibyte emoji, so the UTF-8 decode fails before we reassemble the JSON.

lena: snippet from logs (simplified):
```
chunk A: '{"choices":[{"text":"I love \ud83c\udf4e'
chunk B: 's","index":0}]}'
```
We're using URLSession dataTask didReceive with a byte buffer. When app resumes, incoming chunks sometimes contain only half the emoji.

maya: are you treating SSE keepalives? per spec some servers send lines starting with ':' — we usually ignore those and keep buffering. if you drop a partial line you can lose bytes. which handler do you use?

lena: dataTask + didReceive. We strip out lines that start with ':' immediately when they arrive — maybe that's the bug, because a keepalive can arrive splitting a JSON boundary and we accidentally discard the remainder.

devon: two quick suggestions: (1) never drop raw bytes until you've determined they're part of a complete event; handle keepalive as a line but if it interrupts a non-terminated buffer, stash it and recompose. (2) use an incremental UTF-8 decoder and only attempt JSON parse when you see a full object boundary (e.g. trailing \n or closing brace) or a complete NDJSON line. Pseudocode: 
```
buffer.append(data)
while let end = findJSONBoundary(buffer) {
  let slice = buffer.prefix(upTo: end)
  // decode explicitly, fallback to incremental decode on failure
  let str = String(decoding: slice, as: UTF8.self)
  try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(str.utf8))
  buffer.removeFirst(end)
}
```
If the UTF8 decode fails, keep the bytes and wait for the next chunk — do not drop or substitute.

sam: also add a short backpressure safeguard: if the buffer grows > 512KB without a boundary, pause reads or apply a hard fail to avoid memory blowup. For iOS URLSession you can throttle by coalescing didReceive calls and scheduling parsing on a serial queue.

maya: good call. we should also add a small regression test that intentionally splits multibyte characters and interleaves keepalives. stream-test-bot can send configurable split points.

stream-test-bot: scheduled test run: iOS-split-emoji-keepalive at 2026-03-17T15:40Z — will post logs to https://ci.example/reports/ios-stream-splits/1932109876 (temporary link).

lena: I'll run the new client branch against that harness in ~30m and report back. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sam: if you want, I can add an incremental UTF8 wrapper in the iOS SDK crate so other teams benefit. quick PR after lunch.

lena: awesome — appreciate it.
